rules.title: Code edition is set by permit application date
rules.plain_english: The building standards that apply to a project are the ones in effect locally on the date the building permit application is submitted (plan-check submittal), not the date of issuance or construction.
rules.applies_to: All permitted construction
rules.verbatim_quote: (a) Only those building standards approved by the commission, and that are effective at the local level at the time an application for a building permit is submitted, shall apply to the plans and specifications for, and to the construction

Some building departments treat production-home plan review as the permit application (CALBO).

rules.title: Permit expiration and code lock-in: 12 months / 180 days
rules.plain_english: Under state law (H&S 18938.6, AB 2913) a building permit remains valid if work starts within 12 months after it is issued, unless the work is abandoned; the building official may grant written extensions of up to 180 days each on a written request showing justifiable cause. If work does not start within 12 months or is abandoned, the permit expires and the code edition in effect at application is lost. Locally adopted CBC/CRC Chapter 1 Section 105.5 adds a 180-day suspension/abandonment rule once work has started; check the local ordinance.

parameters.extension_request: written request by permittee showing justifiable cause; building official may grant one or more extensions in writing (H&S 18938.6)
parameters.code_edition_lock_lost_if: work not commenced within 12 months or abandoned

rules.applies_to: All building permits
rules.citation: Health & Safety Code 18938.5(b)(2)(B), 18938.6 (AB 2913, Stats. 2018 ch. 655); CBC (Part 2) Chapter 1 Div. II Sec. 105.5; CRC R105.5
rules.verbatim_quote: Every permit shall remain valid for purposes of this part if the work on the site authorized by that permit is commenced within 12 months after its issuance, unless the permittee has abandoned the work authorized by the permit.
rules.notes: Statute text seen only through WebSearch excerpts of the DGS "California Building Standards Law" compilation (eff. 2026-01-01) and leginfo; dgs.ca.gov and leginfo cannot be fetched directly. H&S 18938.6(b): "A permittee may request an extension of a permit. The building official may grant, in writing, one or more extensions of time for periods of not more than 180 days per extension. The permittee shall request an extension pursuant to this subdivision in writing and demonstrate justifiable cause for the extension." BSC IB 19-03: AB 2913 "amended HSC Section 18938.5 (b)(2)(B) by changing the exception relative to the permit expiration time period from 180 days to 12 months" and DGS says HSC 18938.5/18938.6 take precedence over the administrative building standards on permit expiration. When work counts as "commenced" is not defined in these excerpts; local amendments still govern suspension/abandonment after start (e.g., 180 days between approved inspections).

verification.correction: 12-month figure confirmed, but the rule misstated the structure. Under H&S 18938.6 (added by AB 2913, eff. 2019-01-01), a permit stays valid if work is commenced within 12 months after issuance unless abandoned, and the building official may grant written extensions of up to 180 days each on a written request showing justifiable cause; under 18938.5(b)(2)(B) the code-edition lock-in is lost if work does not commence within 12 months of the permit date or is abandoned. DGS states that H&S 18938.5 and 18938.6 take precedence over the administrative building standards on permit expiration, so a locally adopted CBC 105.5 cannot impose a 180-day commencement period; the 180-day figure is the CBC 105.5 suspension/abandonment-after-start period and the statutory extension length. Parameters, plain_english and citation updated; effective date 2019-01-01 confirmed.

rules.title: Common work exempt from a building permit
rules.plain_english: A building permit is required to construct, alter, repair, move, demolish or change occupancy of a building, but the code exempts minor work such as a one-story detached shed or playhouse up to 120 sq ft, fences up to 7 ft (swimming pool barriers are not exempt), and retaining walls up to 4 ft measured from the bottom of the footing to the top of the wall, unless the wall supports a surcharge or impounds Class I, II or IIIA liquids. Exempt work still has to meet code, and electrical/plumbing/mechanical work may still need its own permit.

rules.title: Caltrans encroachment permit for work in state highway right-of-way
rules.plain_english: Anyone other than a Caltrans contractor must get a Caltrans encroachment permit before any work or activity within, under or over the state highway right-of-way (driveways, utility cuts, staging, traffic control, landscaping). rules.title: Human remains found: stop work and call the coroner
rules.plain_english: If human remains are discovered anywhere other than a dedicated cemetery, stop all work at the site and nearby areas immediately and contact the county coroner. The coroner has two working days to examine; if remains are Native American, the coroner notifies the Native American Heritage Commission within 24 hours, which notifies the most likely descendant, who has 24 hours to recommend treatment.

rules.title: C-57 license required for water, monitoring and geothermal wells
rules.plain_english: Only a person holding a C-57 Water Well Contractor license may dig, bore, drill, deepen, reperforate, abandon or destroy a water well, cathodic protection well, groundwater monitoring well, or geothermal heat exchange well. Many county environmental health departments also require a well permit and fee.

rules.title: File DWR Well Completion Report within 60 days
rules.plain_english: Whoever constructs, alters or destroys a water, cathodic protection, monitoring or geothermal heat exchange well must file a Well Completion Report (DWR 188) with the Department of Water Resources within 60 days after completing the work, online through OSWCR. Failure to file is a misdemeanor and grounds for CSLB discipline.
